claims.evidence: The witness identified an automatic transmission but could not confirm the specific model or engine compatibility.
Origin cannot be determined from photos of the unit alone without shipping documentation.
The unit is shown detached; no functional test or diagnostic report was provided.
No odometer reading from the donor vehicle or service history is present.
The witness noted a weathered casing; seal integrity and bolt factory markings were not specifically confirmed.

risks.risk: Incompatibility with specific vehicle (M272 engines use various 722.9 or 722.6 variants).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped serial number and model code on the side of the transmission casing.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic core for scrap or parts.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical wear or burnt clutch packs.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the transmission fluid on a white cloth or a video of the input shaft being rotated manually.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a total internal rebuild.

risks.risk: Faulty electronic conductor plate or solenoids.
risks.proof: A diagnostic scan report showing no stored fault codes in the Transmission Control Module (TCM).
risks.if_unproven: as having a defective electronic control unit.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the identification plate or stamped 14-digit serial number on the transmission housing.
Photo of the transmission fluid color and clarity.
Photo of the electrical connector pins to check for oil intrusion or damage.
response.reason: While the item is confirmed as a transmission, the specific model number is required to determine which Mercedes-Benz vehicle it fits. Without the serial number, it cannot be priced accurately for the Abuja market.
